paper.title: Privacy-Preserving Dynamic Personalized Pricing with Demand Learning

settings.name_in_paper: Privacy-preserving dynamic personalized pricing, general (obliviously adversarial) personal information
unmapped: Dynamic pricing: action is a price p in [0,1]; feature phi(x_t,p) known map; reward is revenue p*f(phi^T theta*) where demand follows a GLM in the exponential family
Anticipating (eps,delta)-differential privacy (joint DP) of future prices with respect to each customer's (x_t, y_t)
Demand bounded |y_t| <= B_Y and dispersion parameter zeta in [1/G, G]; learner knows B_Y and G
Personal information x_t chosen by an oblivious adversary before the process starts
settings.definition_quote: In the most general setting, the features $\{x_t\}_{t=1}^T$ of the $T$ customers are arbitrarily chosen before the pricing process starts. ... $\Pr[y_t=y|p_t,x_t,\theta^*] = \exp\{\zeta(y\phi_t^\top\theta^*-m(\phi_t^\top\theta^*)) + h(y)\}$

settings.name_in_paper: Privacy-preserving dynamic personalized pricing with stochastic contexts (Assumption 1)
unmapped: Dynamic pricing: action is a price p in [0,1]; reward is revenue p*f(phi(x,p)^T theta*) with GLM demand
Contexts i.i.d. with E[phi phi^T] >= kappa_x I under uniform prices (non-degenerate)
settings.definition_quote: There exists an underlying distribution $\mu_x$ and a constant $\kappa_x>0$ such that, $x_1,\cdots,x_T\overset{i.i.d.}{\sim}\mu_x$, and furthermore ... $\mathbb E_{(x,p)\sim\mu_x\times U[0,1]}\big[\phi(p,x)\phi(p,x)^\top\big]\succeq \kappa_x I_d$.

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual pricing under standard (eps,delta)-differential privacy (lower bound)
unmapped: Standard (eps,delta)-differential privacy of the entire price sequence including p_t (not anticipating)
settings.definition_quote: a randomized algorithm $A$ satisfies $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differential privacy if for every pair of neighboring databases $D,D'$ and measurable set $\mathcal A\subseteq [\underline p,\overline p]^T$, it holds that $\Pr[A(D)\in\mathcal A]\leq e^{\varepsilon}\Pr[A(D')\in\mathcal A] + \delta$.

source.label: prop:anticipating-linear-regret
source.quote: Let $\pi$ be a contextual pricing policy over $T$ periods that satisfies $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differential privacy as defined in Definition \ref{defn:eps-delta-privacy}, with $\varepsilon<\ln(2)$ and $\delta<1/4$. Then the worst case regret of $\pi$ is lower bounded by $\Omega(T)$.

results.notes: Similar to Claim 13 of Shariff & Sheffet; algorithm class is all standard-DP policies.
